title: 黑色亚特兰蒂斯：种植园世

zh: 黑色亚特兰蒂斯：种植园世
en: Black Atlantis: the plantationocene

zh: 阿伊莎·哈米德
en: AYESHA HAMEED

zh: 这是我在沃克庄园的第一个傍晚。这里曾是甘蔗种植园，如今是奶牛场。正值黄昏。
en: This is my first evening at Walker’s, once a sugar plantation and now a dairy. It is dusk.

zh: 我走出公寓，爬上微微生苔的台阶，向右转入泛紫的光里。左侧是马厩，身后是房屋，面前是草地。
en: I step outside of the flat, climb the slightly mossy stairs and turn right into the purpling light. To my left are horse stables, behind me is the house and in front of me are fields of grass.

zh: 青蛙的声音在黄昏开始，越来越响。我走着的铺砌车道在田野处结束，我右转上一条土路。小径两侧的草很长。当我走到左侧一棵孤树时，小径沿一段小坡向下延伸，继续伸向远处一排树木。右边是南方，远处有几点闪烁的灯光。一只小蝙蝠从我头顶掠过。
en: The sound of the frogs begins at dusk and it gets louder. The paved drive I am walking on ends at the field, and I turn right onto a dirt path. The grass is long on either side of the path. When I reach a lone tree to my left, the path dips down a small hill and continues to a line of trees in the distance. To the right is the South and there are some twinkling lights in the distance. A small bat swoops over my head.

zh: 在青蛙那怪异而尖利的嗡鸣之下，有一种寂静。一只黑狗从大宅跑向我，又转身回去，边跑边回头看我，仿佛想让我跟它走。我离开它，走进长草中倾听。
en: Underneath the alien and screechy whir of the frogs there is a silence. A black dog runs up to me from the big house and then turns around and goes back, looking back at me as if trying to get me to follow it. I walk away from it and into the long grass and listen.

zh: 青蛙更响了。天空变黑。
en: The frogs get louder. The sky turns black.

zh: 另一个开端：现在是两点半，我在哈里森洞穴外的停车场里等了大约三十分钟。旅游大巴和包租出租车高效地进出停车位，装卸着美国游客。
en: Another beginning: it is half past two and I’ve been waiting in the parking lot outside Harrison’s Cave for about thirty minutes. Tour buses and hired taxis efficiently pull in and out of the parking spaces, loading and unloading their American passengers.

zh: 两个男人在我旁边聊天，其中一个让另一个搭车，他们走向一辆涂得鲜艳的公交车。我估计还要等二十分钟。
en: Two men are chatting beside me, one of them offers the other one a lift and they walk over to a brightly painted bus. I figure I have twenty minutes more to wait.

zh: 我听到一声巨响，从书上抬起头，看见一辆柴油小巴飞驰穿过停车场，像抢劫案里的逃逸车。它仓促地斜停在我坐着的公交站附近。车上的牌子只写着“City”。人们迅速下车，柴油引擎轰隆作响。
en: I hear a loud noise and look up from my book to see a diesel-powered minibus hurtling through the lot like a getaway car for a heist. It abruptly stops at a hasty angle near the bus stop where I am sitting. The sign on the bus just says ‘City’. People climb out quickly with the diesel engine rumbling.

zh: 我上车时，公交车又加速得那么快，我踉跄跌到座位上。我撑起身，向司机递出两元巴巴多斯币，带着歉意的“不好意思”，副驾驶座上的男人不耐烦地挥手让我坐下。
en: As I climb the stairs the bus speeds up again so fast I trip onto a seat. I pull myself up holding out my two Barbadian dollars to the driver with an apologetic ‘excuse me’ and the man in the passenger seat waves impatiently at me to sit down.

zh: 车窗外，小巴沿着在甘蔗田中被开凿出的土路飞驰，田野上洒满阳光与尘土。我们尖啸着在另一个站停下，引擎低沉地咕哝又咆哮。
en: I look out of the window as the bus hurtles down dirt roads hewn through fields of cane speckled with sun and dust. We screech to another stop and the engine grumbles and roars.

zh: 外面是甘蔗田，男男女女在路边等候。
en: Outside are the fields of cane, and men and women waiting on the side of the road.

zh: 气候变化与种植园经济之间是什么关系？这是对许多事物的探索——《黑色亚特兰蒂斯》这部持续进行的表演的第四章开端，走访三角贸易三个停靠点之一的腹地，并认真对待唐娜·哈拉维与安娜·青使用“种植园世”一词的方式：它把种植园式生产的发展与我们当前所处地质纪元的开端联系起来。
en: What is the relationship between climate change and plantation economies? This is an exploration of many things – the beginnings of a fourth chapter of an ongoing performance called

, visiting the heartland of one of the three stops of the triangular trade, and taking seriously Donna Haraway’s and Anna Tsing’s use of the term ‘Plantationocene’, which connects the development of a plantation form of production to the beginning of the geological era that we are currently in.

zh: “种植园世”是农业与这个被称为人类世的时代之间关系的占位符。但他们所想的农业类型，是种植园那种工厂式榨取结构对多样农耕方式、森林与牧场的暴力取代——为出口而种植甘蔗和棉花等单一作物，由被强行跨越遥远距离运来、遭奴役或受契约束缚的劳动者身体生产。种植园消灭所栽培之物的多样性，摧毁土地，暴力剥削与剥夺在土地上劳作的身体，并摧毁居住在这些地区者任何可能的自给自足的自主性。
en: The ‘Plantationocene’ is a placeholder for the relationship between agriculture and this era, called the Anthropocene. But the kind of agriculture they are thinking about is the violent replacement of diverse farming tactics, of forests and of pastures, by the factory-like extractive structure of plantations – the cultivation of single crops like sugar and cotton for export, produced by enslaved and indentured labouring bodies forcibly transported across vast distances. Plantations eradicate the diversity of what is cultivated, devastating the land, violently exploiting and expropriating the bodies working on the land and destroying any possible autonomy for self-sustenance for those living in these areas.

zh: ［我们使用］“种植园世”一词，指对人类照料的多样农场、牧场与森林的毁灭性转化，转变为榨取性的、圈围的种植园，依赖奴隶劳动以及其他被剥削、被异化、通常被空间运输的劳动……为资本积累与利润而将物质—符号的生成能力转移到世界各地——迅速迁移并重新组合种质、基因组、插条，以及其他各种名称与形式的生物体片段和被连根拔起的植物、动物与人——是种植园世、资本世与人类世共同的一项界定性操作。
en: [we use the term] Plantationocene for the devastating  transformation of diverse kinds of human-tended farms, pastures,  and forests into extractive and enclosed plantations, relying on  slave labor and other forms of exploited, alienated, and usually  spatially transported labor… Moving material semiotic generativity  around the world for capital accumulation and profit – the rapid  displacement and reformulation of germ plasm, genomes, cuttings,  and all other names and forms of part organisms and of deracinated plants, animals, and people – is one defining operation of the  Plantationocene, Capitalocene, and Anthropocene taken together.

zh: “种植园世”表明，人类对地球生态系统施加的地质力量根源于种植园奴隶制，根源在于它把土壤工具化为单一生产，并暴力奴役身体，用作栽培和收获甘蔗的机器，理想状态下还自我繁殖与维持。正如安娜·青所说，“种植园世”由“复制机器”或“简化的生态，如种植园，在其中生命世界被重制为未来资产”构成——换言之，它凸显一次激进暴力侵入的后果及其对交织人类与自然的生命世界的影响。
en: The Plantationocene suggests that the geological force of humans on the planet’s ecosystem had its roots in plantation slavery, its instrumentalization of the soil for a singular kind of production and its violent enslavement of bodies to be used as machines to cultivate and harvest the cane, and to ideally reproduce and sustain itself. As Anna Tsing says, the Plantationocene is formed of ‘machines of replication’ or ‘simplified ecologies, such as plantations, in which life worlds are remade as future assets’ – in other words it highlights the aftermath of a radical and violent incursion and its effects on lifeworlds that intertwine the human and the natural.

zh: 要读取三百多年种植园及其不断演变的社会关系的历史——它紧随最古老的种植园奴隶制实例而来，且奴隶、种植园主与监工的后代仍然在场——并将其对置于标记气候变化的缓慢时间摆动，这几乎是不可能的努力。把一段仍然活着、仍在场的历史，对置于一个缓慢展开的、自然灾害频率增加、海洋变暖、海洋生命受威胁的未来，是不可通约的，也许毫无意义，因为它们运行在如此不同的层面，而在地面层面找到共同基础的可能性几乎为零。
en: It is an almost impossible endeavour to read a history of over three hundred years of plantations and their continually evolving social relations in the wake of the oldest instance of plantation slavery, and in the continued presence of descendants of slaves and plantation owners and overseers, against the slow temporal swings that mark climate change. Reading a still living and present history against a slowly unravelling future of increasing frequencies of natural disaster, the warming of the ocean, the jeopardization of sea life is incommensurable and probably pointless as they operate in such different registers, and the possibility of finding common ground at ground level is nearly nil.

zh: 一天又一天，上午有太阳，下午有太阳，然后雨从天空劈开一道口子。雨季刚刚结束，边缘处仍有水的威胁。偏偏就在今天，这占据了中心舞台。出租车开到大宅前。雨点硕大而饱满，根本不可能冲上台阶钻进车门而不被淋湿。
en: After day after day after day of sun in the morning, sun in the afternoon, rain sliced through the sky in a gash. The rainy season has just ended and at the margins there is still the threat of water. This has taken centre stage, today of all days. The taxi drives up to the house. The rain is so fat and plummy that it is impossible to sprint up the steps to the car door without getting wet.

zh: 出租车驶近城市边缘，雨刷勉强清出视野。每一下刮动都发出刺耳的声响。我们经过码头，所有远洋客轮都停泊在那里，它们庞大的船身在瓢泼大雨的浓密中模糊不清。然后我们到达亚特兰蒂斯办公室。它色彩鲜艳，满是游客纪念品：朗姆酒与海滩、杯垫与钥匙扣。角落里有免费的水果潘趣酒。墙上一幅壁画，一扇画出来并镶嵌装饰得像珊瑚墙的窗户。房间两边各有一台电视——一台循环播放潜艇的纪录片宣传片，另一台锁定CNN，无休止循环着特朗普在十二月下旬赢得选举人团投票。
en: The taxi approaches the outskirts of the city with the wipers barely clearing the view. Each stroke of the blades makes a grating sound. We drive past the terminal where all the ocean liners anchor, their bulky bodies indistinct in the distance with the thickness of the pelting water. And then we arrive at the Atlantis office. It is brightly coloured and full of tourist memorabilia: rum and beaches, coasters and keychains. There is some free fruit punch in the corner. On the wall is a mural, a window painted and encrusted to look like a coral wall. There is a television on each side of the room – one with a looping documentary promo on the submarine, the other tuned into CNN, an endless loop of Trump winning the Electoral College vote in late December.

zh: 我们等着。
en: We wait.

zh: 一对不堪重负的父母试图让穿着相同衣服的女儿们平静下来——看样子是她们的生日。一车车游客到来，他们纵容地看着两个孩子，或者看CNN。我们都坐在紫色皮长椅上。窗外雨鞭打玻璃。
en: Two overwhelmed parents try to keep their identically dressed daughters calm on what appears to be their birthday. Busloads of tourists arrive and they watch these two children indulgently, or look at CNN. We all sit on purple leather benches. Outside the rain lashes at the windows.

zh: 门终于开了，我们被引导出去，步行一百米到等候的船。雨太大了，他们分发雨伞，要我们合用。即便如此，我到达船边时已浑身湿透。经过安全演示和一阵震耳的音乐，我们出发了。水是灰的，天空也是灰的。雨密密地打在窗上，海景化成模糊的像素。最后我们到达水中央一个点，一个金属小结构从水下伸出。我们到了亚特兰蒂斯潜艇。
en: Finally the door opens and we are ushered out to walk the 100 metres to the waiting boat. It is raining so hard that we are instructed to share the umbrellas they hand out to us. Still, I am drenched by the time I get to the boat. After a safety demonstration, and lots of loud music, we head off. The water is grey and the sky is also grey. The rain falls so thick on the window that the seascape falls into blurry pixels. Finally we arrive at a point in the middle of the water where a small metal structure protrudes from underwater. We’ve arrived at the Atlantis Submarine.

zh: 二十世纪初，约翰·欧内斯特·威廉森——一位英国船长的儿子——被关于失落亚特兰蒂斯以及牙买加皇家港之类海盗城镇沉没的故事所激发。他与兄弟乔治设计并建造了一个他称为“摄影球”的结构：一个带玻璃板的水下室，用同心环制成的管道连接到水面上的船。
en: In the early twentieth century John Ernest Williamson, son of an English sea captain, was fuelled by the stories about lost Atlantises and the sinking of pirate towns like Port Royal in Jamaica. With his brother George he designed and built a structure he called the photosphere, an underwater chamber with a glass panel, which was connected to a boat on the surface of the water by a tube made of concentric rings.

zh: 威廉森搬到巴哈马建造他的摄影球，因为周围水域很浅，珊瑚沙闪闪发白。海水基本没有造成浑浊的浮游植物，因此清澈。摄影球被用于多种目的：作为拍摄最早水下活动影像的舱室，作为旅游新奇事物——游客可以通过水下邮局从海底寄明信片——据说还用于水下打捞沉船。正是在这里拍摄了1916年的《海底两万里》，人影幽灵般静止。1954年的电影也是在这里拍摄的。
en: Williamson moved to the Bahamas to build his photosphere as the surrounding waters are shallow, and the coral sand is sparkling and white. The sea is largely free of clouding phytoplankton, so the water is clear. The photosphere was used for a number of purposes, as a chamber to film the first underwater moving images, as a tourist novelty, where visitors could send postcards from the bottom of the sea through an underwater post office, and reportedly to salvage ships underwater. It is here that the 1916 film of
was filmed, the figures ghostly still. So was the film made in 1954.

zh: 克里斯塔·A. 汤普森描述说，这些早期对摄影球的潜入如梦似幻，但水下景象也被感知为险恶。这反映在威廉森自己的思考中：他四处以题为“美与悲剧”的讲座呈现其海洋工作。巴哈马土地并不特别肥沃，但其海洋生命繁荣、丰富、不断繁殖。
en: Krista A. Thompson describes how these early immersions into the photosphere were dreamlike, but that the vista of the underwater was also perceived to be menacing. This was reflected in Williamson’s own thinking as he travelled to present his work on the sea in a lecture titled ‘Beauty and Tragedy’. Bahamian land was not remarkably fertile but its marine life was blooming and rich and multiplying.

zh: 十九世纪晚期，水下生命作为一种奇观，作为精英的消遣而兴盛。年轻的黑人男子会潜入海底，为在船上等待的淑女们抓取纪念品，她们透过“热带长柄眼镜”窥视大海。海底世界被视为一座水下花园、一片风景或一座森林。
en: In the late nineteenth century underwater life as a kind of spectacle flourished as an elite pastime. Young black men would dive to the bottom of the sea to grab mementos for genteel women waiting on boats, who peered into the sea through ‘tropical lorgnons’. The submarine world was seen as an underwater garden, a landscape or a forest.

zh: 哈钦森……把珊瑚海绵重新想象为“迎客的棕榈”，把鱼想象为“蜂鸟”，把珊瑚想象为“大树”与“庄严的森林”……查尔斯·艾夫斯也认为，海底景观呈现的相似关系，犹如“广袤而壮丽的热带森林——终年披绿，优雅的藤蔓点缀其间，各色花朵繁盛，羽色纷呈、羽毛丰美的无数鸟儿鸣声不绝——与一位女士小而奢华的闺房之间的关系；闺房中有常青枝条、攀援藤蔓，以及关在镀金小笼中的鸟儿”。
en: Hutchinson … re-envisioned coral sponges as ‘welcoming palms,’ fish  as ‘hummingbirds,’ and coral as ‘great trees’ and ‘stately forests’…  Charles Ives also contended that the seascape bore similarity to  ‘the vast and magnificent tropical forests, clothed in perennial  green, adorned with graceful vines, teeming with flowers of every  hue, and vocal with countless birds of the most varied and of the  richest plumage, bear to a lady’s little but luxurious boudoir, with its  evergreen branches, climbing vines and captive birds in their small  but gilded cages.’

zh: 杰茜卡·莱曼描述了1738年荷兰奴隶船
在苏里南海岸外大西洋水域的沉没。船长钉死了关押680名妇女、男人与儿童的货舱舱口。尽管有充分文献记录，残骸从未被找到。在把海洋深处思考为档案时，她写道：
en: Jessica Lehman describes the sinking of the Dutch slave ship

in Atlantic waters off the coast of Suriname in 1738. The captain nailed shut the hatches to the hold of the ship which held 680 women, men and children. Although well documented, the wreck has not been found. In thinking of the ocean depths as archive, she writes:

zh: 如果说海洋掩盖了奴隶制的一些废墟，它却没有那么轻易地隐藏资本主义帝国主义晚近的全部痕迹。1964年7月，在漫长海洋有毒倾倒历史中的一幕里，英国商船
开始把来自数个国营场址的放射性废物包倒入比斯开湾。
en: If the ocean has concealed some of slavery’s ruins, it has not so readily  hidden all of the more recent traces of capitalist imperialism. In July  1964, during one episode in a long history of marine toxic dumping,  the British merchant vessel
began to discard packages of  radioactive waste from several state-operated sites into the Bay of  Biscay.

zh: 放射性废物、手套和瓶子留下了更多痕迹，然而早在1964年之前，就已有一段可观的毒物倾倒史。她把这与葬在
船体中的奴隶联系起来：海洋是一个由废墟界定的储藏库与档案。放射性瓶子漂浮在水面，而按照爱德华·格利桑的讲述，它们的对应物是大西洋海底的洋流，“由‘几乎未腐蚀’的铁球与锁链标示”。
en: The items of radioactive waste, gloves and bottles left more of a trace, and yet even in 1964 were preceded by a substantial history of toxic dumping. This she sees as connected to the slaves buried in the

hull, the ocean a repository and archive defined by ruin. The radioactive bottles float on the surface, and, following Edouard Glissant’s telling, their counterparts are the Atlantic’s under-sea currents, ‘signposted by “scarcely corroded” balls and chains’.

zh: 然后是那些被腐蚀的洋流本身，是2010年深水地平线漏油事故后掺杂着石油的波浪；在那场事故中，210加仑石油与天然气顺着大陆坡滑入深水。这个亚特兰蒂斯不是死者、放射性物质、浮油与腐蚀之物的档案。它
所有这些。这是它的悲剧，也许也是它的美。
en: And then there are the corroded currents themselves, waves laced with oil after the Deepwater Horizon oil spill in 2010 where 210 gallons of oil and natural gas slicked down the continental slope into deep water. This Atlantis is not an archive of the dead, the radioactive, the oil slicked and the corroded. It
all these things. This is its tragedy and maybe its beauty.
body.review: 编者说明：底本写作“210加仑”，译文照录。该数值明显存在数量级疑点：NOAA损害评估与修复项目页记载，深水地平线事故约有1.34亿加仑石油泄入海湾。此处仅提示底本数字问题，不把事故总泄漏量直接等同于原句所述进入深水的数量，也不替作者补定数字。 https://darrp.noaa.gov/oil-spills/deepwater-horizon

zh: 十二年后，亚伦来接我，开车环岛时我们重逢。我们决定去大西洋海岸，这是两次出行中的第一次。这像是一组地名逐渐缩短的旅程：第一次我们开车去一个叫巴斯谢巴的村庄，第二次去海岸另一处叫巴斯的地方。我确信，如果我们第三次出行，会招来第三个叫“巴”的地段。但这种糟糕的幽默不能持久。
en: I meet Aaron after twelve years when he picks me up for a drive around the island. We decide to go to the Atlantic coast, the first of two trips. It seems like a set of journeys of attrition as during the first trip we drive to a village called Bathsheba, and the second time to another part of the coast called Bath. I’m convinced that had we made a third trip it would have conjured a third stretch called Ba. But this kind of bad humour can’t hold.

zh: 大西洋海岸是岛上狂野的海岸。这里水面波涛汹涌，聚落更零散，道路更间断、更蜿蜒。我们开车经过一条阳光铺洒的路，看见一个女人耐心地在路边等候。亚伦停下车，提出载她去上班的地方，结果是一家叫圆屋的临水餐厅，据说鸡尾酒很棒。你原本打算怎么去？他问她，她指向一条消失在长草中的小径。不是什么好主意，他说，我们朝餐厅开去，她同意。下车挥手时她喊道：下一杯鸡尾酒我请。
en: The Atlantic coast is the wild coast of the island. The water here is choppy, the settlements more sporadic and the roads more intermittent and winding. As we drive through a sunny road we see a woman waiting patiently at the side. Aaron stops and offers her a lift to where she works, which turns out to be a restaurant called the Roundhouse on the water, which apparently serves great cocktails. How were you planning to get there? he asks her, and she points to a tiny path that disappears in the long grass. Not a great idea, he says, as we drive to the restaurant and she agrees. The next cocktail is on me, she calls, as she climbs out of the car and waves.

zh: 我第一次跳进大西洋，感到水在拉扯与推挤我的皮肤。水温暖而回旋。脚下的沙石多而粗粝。海滩空无一人。我身后的沙地里，间隔立着木桩，是曾经沿海岸运输甘蔗的铁路残迹。海岸自那时起已后退，曾经环绕干地的木桩如今半淹没在水中。
en: The first time I jump in the Atlantic I feel the water pull and push against my skin. It is warm and swirling. The sand below my feet is rocky and rough. The beach is empty. Behind me in the sand are stumps of wood periodically placed, remnants of a railway track used to transport sugar along the coast. The coast has receded since then and the stumps which once circled dry land are now half underwater.

zh: 我向东望去，越过水面，看不见任何陆地。亚伦顺着我的目光，告诉我下一片陆地是塞内加尔海岸。我继续盯着东方。
en: I look to the east, across the water and see that there is no land in sight. Following my gaze, Aaron tells me that the next land mass is the Senegalese coast. I keep staring east.

zh: 2006年4月29日，一艘二十英尺长的船在巴巴多斯东南海岸的拉格德角外被发现。海岸警卫队在船上发现十一具尸体，被阳光与海水保存并风干。这是一艘在大西洋上漂流了四个月的幽灵船。它在圣诞日从佛得角群岛的普拉亚启航，满载来自塞内加尔、几内亚比绍和冈比亚的移民，前往加那利群岛。每个人都为船上的位置付了890英镑。
en: On 29 April 2006 a twenty-foot boat was spotted off Ragged Point on the south-eastern coast of Barbados. On board eleven bodies were found by the coastguards, preserved and desiccated by the sun and salt water. This was a ghost ship adrift for four months on the Atlantic Ocean. It set sail on Christmas Day in Praia in the Cape Verde Islands full of migrants from Senegal, Guinea Bissau and Gambia en route to the Canary Islands. Each of these people paid £890 for their place on the boat.

zh: 船在毛里塔尼亚港口努瓦迪布遇到麻烦，曾被另一艘船拖行一段时间。《卫报》一篇文章推测，拖缆可能是被砍刀砍断的。一旦漂流，船便开始横越大西洋的缓慢移动，受风雨冲击，被洋流拉向西。到一月，所有乘客都已死亡；许多人的尸体被抛入海中或从船上冲落。这艘幽灵船随后航行了2,800英里，抵达巴巴多斯。
en: The boat ran into trouble at Nouadhibou, a Mauritian port, and was towed for a time by another ship. An article in the

conjectures that the line was possibly severed by being hacked by a machete. Once adrift the boat began its slow movement across the Atlantic, buffeted by the winds and rain, and pulled westward by the ocean’s currents. By January all the passengers had died; many of their bodies were jettisoned into the sea or washed overboard. This ghost ship then travelled the 2,800 miles to Barbados.
body.review: 编者说明：底本将努瓦迪布称为Mauritian港口（毛里求斯的）；该章所引《卫报》原报道写作Mauritanian（毛里塔尼亚的），译文据此作“毛里塔尼亚”。 https://www.theguardian.com/world/2006/may/29/gilestremlett.mainsection

zh: 船上发现的一封死于船上者所写的便条，以及一张塞内加尔航空公司的机票，提供了拼图的最初几块。据《卫报》报道，船上还发现了两张便条：
en: A note written by one of the men who died on board and a ticket for a Senagalese Airlines flight found on the boat provided the first pieces of the puzzle. According to the
, these two notes were also found on board:

zh: “我想给我在巴萨达（塞内加尔内陆的一个城镇）的家人寄一笔钱。请原谅我，再见。这是我在这个巨大的摩洛哥海中的生命终点，”据巴巴多斯报纸《每日国民报》报道，便条这样写道。
en: ‘I would like to send to my family in Bassada [a town in the interior  of Senegal] a sum of money. Please excuse me and goodbye. This is  the end of my life in this big Moroccan sea,’ the note said, according  to a Barbados paper, the

zh: “我来自塞内加尔，但在佛得角住了一年。情况很糟。我觉得我活着走不出去了。我需要发现我的人把这笔钱寄给我的家人。请打电话给我的朋友易卜拉希马·德拉梅。
署名：迪奥·松卡尔·迪埃米。” 《国家报》对船上发现便条的记述
en: ‘I am from Senegal but have been living in Cape Verde for a year.  Things are bad. I don’t think I will come out of this alive. I need  whoever finds me to send this money to my family. Please telephone  my friend Ibrahima Drame.
Signed Diaw Sounkar Diemi.’
’s account of note found on boat

zh: 清晨时分，太阳辐射加热陆地比加热海洋更快。陆地上更热、更轻的空气把风从海洋拉向陆地。因此，太阳升起时，岛屿四面都被从海洋吹向内陆的风包围。
en: In the morning hours, radiation from the sun warms the land faster than it warms the sea. The hotter, lighter air of the land pulls the wind from sea to land. So, as the sun rises, the island is surrounded on all sides by winds that blow inland from the sea.

zh: 巴巴多斯只有两种岛上独有的植物，“一种常见沟壑灌木
，有时称为扫帚，以及一种罕见的细长攀援植物
，它没有俗名”。
其余近三千种植物都来自水域彼岸——有些由跨洋船只运来并被暴力栽培，另一些由自然力量带来——由飞越水面的鸟和风带来。
en: Barbados has only two species of plants that are unique to the island, ‘a common gully shrub
sometimes called broom, and a rare slender climber,
, which has no common name’.

The rest of the nearly three thousand varieties of plants came from across the water – some borne on ships from across the ocean and violently cultivated, and others carried by forces of nature – by birds flying across the water and by the wind.

zh: ［在巴巴多斯］植物随风和洋流、在鸟类帮助下抵达海岸。此外，我们许多野生植物是有意引入的，后来变得能自行播种并归化。人们常说，巴巴多斯的许多野生植物是外来的杂草。
en: [In Barbados] flora reach the shores on winds and ocean currents  and with the help of birds. In addition many of our wild plants are  deliberate introductions which have since become self-seeding and  naturalised. It is often said that many of the wild plants of Barbados  are exotic weeds.

zh: 由吹过安的列斯群岛的种子长成的植物，被毁灭性的甘蔗田取代。这些曾遭大量摧毁、由风、洋流与鸟带来的植物，如今在土路两侧、在用作放牧的田野上、在穿过珊瑚洞穴的沟壑中茂密生长。
en: Plants grown from seeds blown across the Antilles were replaced by annihilating fields of sugar cane. These decimated plants, blown by wind and carried by ocean currents and birds, now grow thickly across dirt-hewn paths, on fields grown for grazing, and in gullies carved through coral caves.

zh: 一个更强的风系从更远处吹来。信风横越大西洋吹向加勒比海，携带着天气，数个世纪以来也推送着从东到西的船帆。撒哈拉沙漠的尘土吹过大西洋，把一块大陆的物质一粒一粒地搬到海洋另一侧的一串岛屿上。巴巴多斯是这些尘粒触及的第一片海岸；在春、夏、秋三季，空气充满萨赫勒的物质，大地铺满它的磷光。
en: A stronger system of winds travels from farther away. Trade winds blow across the Atlantic Ocean to the Caribbean Sea, carrying the weather, and for centuries the sails of ships from East to West. Dust from the Sahara Desert blows across the Atlantic, moving grain by grain the matter of one continent onto a line of islands on the other side of the ocean. Barbados is the first coast that these particles of dust touch, and for spring, summer and autumn the air is full of matter of the Sahel, and the earth is carpeted with its phosphorescence.

zh: 本作品的研究得以进行，得益于加拿大艺术委员会颁发的一笔旅行资助，用于参加在特立尼达爱丽丝庭院与巴巴多斯鲜奶驻地项目。
en: Research for this work was made possible by a travel grant awarded by the Canada Council for the Arts to attend residencies at Alice Yard (Trinidad) and Fresh Milk (Barbados).
